item.title: Nashik civic body's special drive to bring more properties under tax net gets poor response
item.description: Starting September 22, the Nashik Municipal Corporation has kicked off a program aimed at registering unassessed properties. Unfortunately, only 30 property owners have stepped forward in the first week. Municipal Commissioner Manisha Khatri stressed the critical need to boost the municipality's revenue through this effort. With more than six lakh properties documented in Nashik, the NMC is particularly focused on locating unregistered ones before the campaign concludes on October 1.

item.title: Panchkula: 130 plot owners yet to clear dues under HSVP settlement scheme
item.description: Haryana Shehri Vikas Pradhikaran has outlined 130 Panchkula plots eligible for enhancement charge settlements, providing an extended deadline of December 31. This one-time settlement option is expected to attract numerous beneficiaries, although some local residents express ongoing concerns regarding the enhancement charges. Eligible plot owners can easily check their rebate status and apply through the HSVP website.

item.title: Bengaluru's BDA apartments yet to fully turn EV infrastructure switch on
item.description: In Bengaluru, the trend of electric vehicle ownership is gaining momentum in apartment communities. A recent survey indicates that merely one in fifteen BDA complexes boasts a communal charging unit. The majority of residents rely on public charging stations or set up home solutions remotely. Notably, there's a strong enthusiasm among potential buyers for EVs in the coming years.

item.title: Set up dedicated sub-registrar office at PMC headquarters: Builders’ association urges Pune civic body
item.description: The Marathi Bandhkam Vyavsayik Association has formally approached the Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) to establish a dedicated property registration office. According to Nitin Deshpande, the association's president, this development promises to streamline the property registration process, benefiting both builders and citizens. PMC is currently reviewing this proposal and will determine its viability while also coordinating with the Registration and Stamps Department for further insights.

item.title: Ease plan approvals for 70 metres buildings, says CREDAI-Ahmedabad
item.description: CREDAI Ahmedabad has urged the state government to streamline the approval process for highrise projects. The association highlighted delays in project timelines due to issues with Transferable Development Rights availability. They proposed a staged approval system separating plan scrutiny from TDR loading requirements. Developers requested that punitive actions not target builders for unrelated traffic issues caused by parking violations.

item.title: Branded PGs & guesthouses set up at homes in Gurugram's Sushant Lok-3 on government radar, 30 served notices
item.description: In Sushant Lok-3, over 30 structures have been flagged for potential enforcement measures due to the operation of unauthorized PGs, guest houses, and commercial activities within residential areas. Local residents are expressing their grievances, particularly about issues related to parking, drainage, and the strain on utilities stemming from these illicit operations.
